problems.problem: The five-minute block the parcel was sent back to kill is STILL THERE on the sibling command, and the report says it is not. Reproduced in a real headless browser at the command level: `deployRemove('legacy', ROOT, {web:true})`, clicked the page's own 'Keep it' button on the confirm-remove view. The click walks back to a listing whose only buttons are ["Edit target","Remove target"] (I read the live DOM) — no cancel, no done, nothing that posts anything — and the run then sat for 300,021 ms before printing 'Kept target legacy.' and returning 0. Same for `capy deploy targets --web`: probing chooseDeployTargetInBrowser in browse mode returned buttons ["Edit target","Remove target","copy","copy"] and an unanswered page rejected with 'Timed out waiting for the browser (5 minutes).' Root cause is in a file this parcel owns and is one line: TOKENS_TIMEOUT_MS was applied only as the default inside showDeployTokensInBrowser, and `grep -n timeoutMs src/commands/deployCommand.ts` is EMPTY — chooseDeployTargetInBrowser is called with timeoutMs undefined from both deployList (~line 998) and deployRemove (~line 1080), so both keep the wizard's 300s default. The report claims 'Same treatment applied to deployList/deployRemove's chooseDeployTargetInBrowser catches' and elsewhere presents the shortened deadline as the thing 'that makes capy deploy list --web a listing again'; only the catch shape was changed. A decline on a destructive command that takes five silent minutes to be acknowledged is the exact rule the commit is named after.

Report claim falsified: 'it gained one additive option (onServed) in src/ui/screens/serve.ts — no other parcel branch touches that file, I checked all six.' web/connectors edits the SAME hunk of the same file with a different mechanism for the same problem — a `readonly delivered: Promise<boolean>` settled from the same res.on('finish') handler. Read-only trial merge: `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only web/deploy web/connectors` → 'CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in src/ui/screens/serve.ts' (plus the expected one in tests/ui/browserFlow.e2e.test.ts). Two parcels have now invented two ways for a caller to learn the page was delivered, in shared infrastructure — the same 'do not invent a second way' objection the reviewer raised about showScreenInBrowser, moved one layer down. The deploy change itself is behaviour-preserving for existing callers (the finish listener is now always registered; closeAfterServe still gates only the close), so this is a coordination/mergeability problem, not a correctness one.

`capy deploy revoke <id> --web` declined still costs the full TOKENS_TIMEOUT_MS before it says anything. Measured end to end with a real browser and a mocked service: clicked 'Leave it active', and the command took 120,017 ms to print 'Nothing revoked — a1b2c3d4e5f6 is still active.' The outcome is now right (exit 0, revokeDeployToken never called) and the true fix is a packages/ui change the parcel may not make and correctly reported in the showDeployTokensInBrowser docstring — but the page itself still shows the user nothing after their decline, so the ending is reached invisibly and two minutes late.

The command-level decline tests ('a cancelled listing changes nothing and exits 0' line 171, 'declining the confirm KEEPS the target and exits 0' line 214) decline by POSTing `{__action:'cancel'}` directly to /submit. No control on deploy-targets produces that payload — the browse view has only Edit/Remove and the confirm view's 'Keep it' sets `view='list'` client-side and posts nothing (packages/ui/screens/deploy-targets/Screen.svelte:248). They pin a vocabulary that is currently unreachable from the page, so they cannot catch the hang in problem #1; only browserFlow.e2e.test.ts:1117 drives a real decline click, and only for deploy-tokens.
